A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HiPPO-based online interdomain Gaussian process work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained, revised, and added material.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original Solar Irradiance and Audio regression experiments, predictive distributions, runtime measurements, and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original time-series, COVID, UCI, ERA5, and toy-study results, including repeated-run uncertainty estimates.

M1.justification: The HiPPO/RFF covariance machinery is retained, but v3 adds a multidimensional-input procedure using actual or constructed observation order (Section 3.3), and an online HiPPO-SVGPVAE with EWC-regularized encoder and decoder (Section 5.3). These are procedural and model extensions beyond the OHSGPR-to-OHSVGP renaming.

E1.justification: v3 retains Solar Irradiance and Audio while adding COVID death-count modeling, Skillcraft and Powerplant continual regression, ERA5 climate prediction through a GPVAE, and Two-moon binary classification. These substantially expand domains, input dimensionality, and task requirements.

E2.justification: The original OSGPR/OVFF comparisons gain OVC and OVC-optZ on Solar/Audio. v3 also evaluates OVC-per-dim in GPVAE experiments and an offline AR(2) Renewal comparator for COVID in Appendix E.1. These are evaluated comparator additions, not merely citations or renamed methods.

E3.justification: For retained fixed-kernel experiments, full-GP calibration changes from the first two tasks to the initial task. v2 specifies 500 training and 5000 testing RFF samples; v3 specifies 1000. New protocols include feature-sorted UCI tasks, COVID evaluation with ECE, and GPVAE training with specified architecture and budgets.

E4.justification: v3 adds posterior-reconstruction analysis, ordering-sensitivity studies, and LegS/LegT/LagT/FouT comparisons (Figure 1 and Appendix E.3–E.4). Conversely, v2's discretization-step and RFF-sample sensitivity grids are removed. The Solar forgetting case study is also reconfigured from intermediate-task snapshots to a final-task comparison.

E5.justification: v2 provides predictive standard-deviation bands but no repeated-run counts or run-based confidence intervals. v3 reports means and 95% confidence intervals from five independent runs, or three for ERA5. This introduces experiment-level uncertainty reporting; it does not establish how many runs were performed for v2.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial COVID, UCI, ERA5, and toy-study results, including reported 100% Two-moon accuracy for random and k-min ordering but forgetting with k-max. Solar/Audio curves and runtime entries change, while detailed sweep results disappear. Changed settings prevent interpreting revised scores as controlled before-and-after performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds a posterior-coefficient mean/covariance derivation and finite-basis result, and Appendix D.2 adds formal SVGPVAE specifications. Equation 3 corrects an inducing-variable mismatch. However, Appendix A changes the displayed HiPPO-LegS diagonal from -(n+1)/t to (-n+1)/t, introducing a mathematical inconsistency.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion broaden the central contribution from long-term time-series regression to multidimensional continual learning and deep generative modeling. GPVAE integration, identified as future work in v2, becomes a claimed and evaluated contribution in v3.

C2.justification: v3 extends the discussion beyond inducing-point drift and OVFF tuning difficulty to ordering dependence, unavailable oracle ordering, forgetting with recency-weighted bases, and instability of continued kernel optimization. It also explains OVFF's early underfitting and offers tentative mechanisms for GPVAE forgetting.

D1.justification: v3 adds inducing-point initialization details, the two-layer MLP and 20-dimensional latent architecture, A6000 hardware information, and renewal/GPVAE specifications. It removes v2's explicit Solar/Audio preprocessing recipe and numerical discretization-step disclosures, replacing preprocessing detail with references. Reproducibility documentation therefore changes substantially in both directions.

R1.justification: New Section 4 distinguishes inducing-variable updates from approximate inference and positions the method against OVC, pivoted-Cholesky, memory-based online GPs, and Markovian GPs. It adds an explicit first-online-interdomain-GP claim and substantial related literature, including Maddox et al. and Chang et al.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganized around three applications and shifts its main emphasis to fixed kernels, with trainable-kernel results in Appendix E.2. Method explanations and section hierarchy are revised, related work becomes a dedicated section, and terminology, authorship, headers, and acknowledgments change.

P2.justification: v3 adds a method illustration, multiple application and ablation figures, and landscape appendix grids. Existing Solar/Audio displays are reorganized; the six-panel Solar case becomes four final-task panels. Table 1 replaces parameter-sweep rows with compact method comparisons and adds COVID columns.

improvement.justification: OVC comparisons, independent-run confidence intervals, and ordering/basis failure analyses substantially strengthen evidence for memory preservation and clarify its boundaries beyond v2's narrow validation. The expanded applications also receive concrete protocols and results. These gains outweigh the lost preprocessing/discretization detail and the introduced Appendix A diagonal inconsistency, although those remain meaningful reproducibility weaknesses.
